항목.프롬프트: Wide illustrated story panel for a children's Bible game, one single full-bleed scene with no border and no frame: many years later on a bright sunny morning, on a green terraced hillside vineyard full of grapevines, a happy Judean family: the father, a bearded man in a long brown wool robe, kneels by a small hole in the earth and lifts up an old sealed clay jar with both hands, the mother in a long blue dress and a white headscarf smiles and holds a basket of grapes, a little girl and a little boy laugh and point at the jar; far away on the horizon the stone walls of Jerusalem are being rebuilt with simple wooden scaffolding and workers carrying stones; no cranes, no machines. All houses are one-story or two-story stone and mud-brick houses with flat earthen rooftops and low parapets; no sloped roofs, no roof tiles. Everyone wears ancient Israelite clothing: long simple wool tunics and robes with cloth sashes, women in long dresses with headscarves, children in short simple tunics, leather sandals; no modern clothes, no t-shirts, no shorts, no trousers, no hats, no metal buckets, no glass windows, no roof tiles; only clay jars and woven baskets. No statues, no idols, no carved figures, no winged discs, no crescent shapes, no moon ornaments, no religious symbols anywhere. Hands are drawn simply and clearly, each hand with four fingers and a thumb, and no hand overlaps another person. Every face is clear and well drawn with distinct eyes, nose and mouth. Every person has exactly two arms, two hands, two legs and two feet.
